_comment: Office Awards: Retirement Edition. A page of light, warm workplace award categories -- 'Keeper of the Spare Phone Charger', 'Calmest Voice on a Busy Shift' -- and for each one a coworker writes the name of the colleague who deserves it. The service writes award titles only; nobody is named and no coworker list is ever sent. Variety is structural: every award gets its own brief -- a theme, one of its details, a tone (playful or warm) and a title shape -- sampled by seed from 23 themes and about 200 details; a set plans different themes, capped per group (one drinks award, one timekeeping award, no pile of meeting jokes), always with one farewell award about the retiree, plus spares for the gates on both sides. subjectWords spot what an award is really about whatever its brief said, so a coffee award written for a teamwork brief still counts as the set's coffee award. qualifierWords, phrases and synonyms fold an award to its underlying idea so 'Most Coffee Consumed' and 'Biggest Coffee Drinker' are one award. Brands are the Bucket List's own list (bucket-list/prompt.json).

locale.nativeLine: - Write in clear, warm, natural English that reads well in both British and American workplaces.
locale.otherLine: - Write every award title in language locale '{locale}', natural for that language, keeping each one short and in title case where the language uses it.

any.label: Any workplace
any.line: The workplace is not known. Use words that work in an office, a school, a hospital, a shop or a workshop alike -- the team, a shift, the break room, the rota, the car park -- and never depend on cubicles, conference rooms or corporate jargon.

office.label: Office or corporate team
office.line: The team works in an office. Desks, email, meetings and the printer are fair game, but keep jargon light and never make every award about office equipment.

school.label: School or college
school.line: The team works at a school or college: teachers, support staff and office staff. The staff room, timetables, the photocopier, the bell, playground duty and school events are fair game. Never joke about pupils or parents.

healthcare.label: Hospital, clinic or care
healthcare.line: The team works in healthcare or care: a hospital, clinic, practice or care home. Shifts, handovers, the staff room, the rota and teamwork on a busy day are fair game. Never joke about patients, illness or anything medical.

service.label: Shop, restaurant or hotel
service.line: The team works in retail, hospitality or customer service: a shop, cafe, restaurant or hotel. Shifts, the stockroom, the till, opening and closing and looking after customers are fair game. Never mock customers.

trades.label: Workshop, site or factory
trades.line: The team works in a workshop, on a site, in a warehouse or a factory. Tools, the tea break, the van, the shift pattern, the canteen and getting the job done are fair game. Never joke about safety or accidents.

tones.playful: playful: an affectionate, recognisable workplace habit the winner would laugh about and be proud of
tones.warm: warm: appreciation for a kindness, strength or quality the team is grateful for

shapes.most-likely: starts with "Most Likely to" and a verb ("Most Likely to Rescue the Photocopier")
shapes.superlative: starts with one superlative such as Best, Fastest, Friendliest, Calmest, Tidiest or Warmest, then the thing ("Friendliest Hello on a Monday")
shapes.title: an honorary title or role the winner holds ("Keeper of the Spare Phone Charger", "Chief Morale Booster")
shapes.named-award: a named award ending in the word Award ("The Never-Without-a-Pen Award")
shapes.habit: a short habit phrase starting with Always, Never Without or First to ("Never Without a Spare Umbrella")
